title: Marketing to Chinese Tourists in 2023 - Where Are They Going?

facts.fact: Chinese tourists made 170 million trips in 2019 alone, according to the page.
facts.quote: In 2019 alone, they made 170 million trips, contributing 254 billion USD to the global economy.

facts.fact: In 2019, Chinese tourists contributed 254 billion USD to the global economy, according to the page.
facts.quote: In 2019 alone, they made 170 million trips, contributing 254 billion USD to the global economy.

facts.fact: According to China Outbound Tourism Research Institute (COTRI), the majority of the initial wave of cross-border travel out of China will likely be urgent non-leisure trips for business, family reunification, student travel, and healthcare.
facts.quote: The majority of the initial wave of cross-border travel out of China will likely be urgent non-leisure trips for business, family reunification, student travel, and healthcare

facts.fact: The full recovery of leisure tourism from China is likely to begin only in the second quarter of 2023, according to the page.
facts.quote: The full recovery of leisure tourism will likely begin only in the second quarter of 2023.

facts.fact: According to Trip.com reservation data, Thailand, Japan, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Singapore are the top destinations for Chinese tourists.
facts.quote: Thailand, Japan, Hong Kong, South Korea, and Singapore top the list

facts.fact: According to Trip.com reservation data, the top long-haul destinations for Chinese tourists are the US, UK, and Australia.
facts.quote: with the US, UK, and Australia being the top destinations for long-haul flights, according to Trip.com reservation data.

facts.fact: According to a 2023 Fitch Ratings analysis, Chinese tourism contributed roughly a third of all tourists for Vietnam, Thailand, and Korea in 2019.
facts.quote: contributing roughly a third of all tourists for countries like Vietnam, Thailand, and Korea

facts.fact: In 2022, most APAC destinations saw a tenfold decrease in Chinese tourist numbers compared to 2019, according to the page.
facts.quote: with 2022 seeing a tenfold decrease in numbers compared to 2019 for most APAC destinations
